name: IL-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: No polling or expert ratings; fundamentals-driven
model.rationale: Bill Foster holds a D+6 seat with a huge financial edge and no outside opposition, while Jeff Walter has raised little and has almost no cash on hand. Markets price a Democratic win near 95%, consistent with the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or a strong national environment shift could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Foster, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this D+6 suburban Chicago district. He has raised over $2.1 million and holds $2.5 million on hand, while Republican Jeff Walter has raised about $311,000 with only $23,000 remaining. No outside groups are active on either side, and no public polls or expert ratings cover the race.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95 percent. With a favorable partisan lean, incumbency, and a dominant financial position, the seat sits firmly in the Democratic column heading into November, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
